themes_detail.label: Massive tree damage spike
themes_detail.summary: Park Slope is experiencing a severe surge in damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK with 19 reports vs. a 2.6-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 624% spike (z-score: 11.62)—suggesting either storm damage, disease, or infrastructure conflict affecting the neighborhood's canopy.
evidence: 19 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (624% increase, z-score: 11.62)
Damaged Tree is among top 10 complaint categories over 90 days with 308 total complaints
Community Board has repeatedly requested park reconstruction/upgrade funding, suggesting existing infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent weather events (wind, ice, heavy snow from last week's snow complaints) triggered tree failures across Park Slope
Interview Parks Department and arborists about disease, pest pressure, or deferred maintenance in district's street trees and parks
Map which neighborhoods/blocks are seeing the spike to identify infrastructure conflicts (sidewalk damage, utility lines, development activity)

themes_detail.label: Street condition deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints in Park Slope surged to 84 THIS WEEK vs. a 17.4-complaint weekly baseline—a 384% spike (z-score: 7.72)—coinciding with winter weather damage and suggesting accelerating pavement failure or pothole creation.
evidence: 84 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 17.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (384% increase, z-score: 7.72)
Snow or Ice complaints were at 1,429 over 90 days, indicating winter weather stress on infrastructure
Street Condition is 7th-highest complaint category overall (394 complaints last 90 days), showing sustained baseline issue
reporting_angles: Determine whether this week's spike correlates with freeze-thaw cycles or specific storm events that cracked roads
Contact NYC DOT to learn repair timelines and whether Park Slope is prioritized for pothole filling this winter
Document specific streets with clusters of complaints to show geographic pattern of deterioration

themes_detail.label: Dead animal complaints triple
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints in Park Slope spiked to 7 THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average—an 833% increase (z-score: 9.45)—signaling either disease outbreak, wildlife conflict, or sanitation breakdown requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 7 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (833% increase, z-score: 9.45)
Rodent complaints also elevated THIS WEEK at 13 vs. 4.0 weekly average (225% increase, z-score: 5.69)
Dirty Condition complaints spiked to 54 THIS WEEK vs. 15.8 weekly average (243% increase), suggesting broader sanitation issues
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health to investigate whether there is a disease or contamination event affecting wildlife in Park Slope
Interview Parks Department and local residents about any visible animal sickness, unusual animal behavior, or possible pesticide use
Cross-reference rodent spike with dead animal spike to assess whether there is a coordinated pest control action or disease driver

themes_detail.label: Dirty conditions surge
themes_detail.summary: Dirty condition complaints jumped to 54 THIS WEEK vs. 15.8 weekly average—a 243% spike (z-score: 4.75)—compounded by 8 dumpster complaints last week (up 540%) and suggesting either sanitation service disruption or waste mismanagement across Park Slope.
evidence: 54 dirty condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 15.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (243% increase, z-score: 4.75)
8 dumpster complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average (540% increase, z-score: 6.97)
Combined with dead animal (7) and rodent (13) spikes, indicates multi-vector sanitation breakdown
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation to determine whether there was a collection delay, holiday schedule disruption, or service reduction in Park Slope this week
Investigate whether commercial construction (1,024 DOB permits filed in past 90 days) is generating excess waste or blocking collection routes
Interview residents and business owners about visible trash accumulation, missed pickups, or illegal dumping

themes_detail.label: Rodent infestation pressure rising
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints in Park Slope hit 13 THIS WEEK vs. 4.0 weekly average—a 225% spike (z-score: 5.69)—coinciding with dead animal and dirty condition surges, suggesting seasonal pest pressure or environmental conditions attracting rodents.
evidence: 13 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (225% increase, z-score: 5.69)
Dead animal and dirty condition complaints also elevated THIS WEEK, suggesting common environmental driver
Community Board has ongoing request for homeless services, which can be correlated with rodent activity in some contexts
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health's pest control unit to learn whether there is an active rodent abatement campaign in Park Slope or if conditions have worsened
Assess whether winter weather is driving rodents indoors and whether residents are reporting building infestations or street-level activity
Interview local business owners about increased pest pressure and whether sanitation/waste management changes have contributed
